ety: So named from Parramatta, in Australia.

senses: Grated yam, a Japanese side dish.
A French labourer or manual worker.
The state currency formerly used in Portugal and its colonies, divided into 100 centavos. The symbol $ is positioned between the escudos and centavos, i.e. 2$50.
The currency formerly used in Chile and replaced by the Peso.
The currency of Cape Verde.
ety: From Portuguese escudo (“shield”) or Spanish escudo. Doublet of scutum, scute, écu, and scudo.

senses: A cocktail of rum, lemon or lime juice and sugar, sometimes with fruit added.
ety: Originated 1915–1920; from Cuban Spanish daiquiri, named after a beach on the south coast of Cuba, from Taíno.

senses: Synonym of crayfish.
ety: Alteration of US and British dialectal crawdab (“crayfish”).

senses: the state or quality of being cooperative
Containing fruit; bearing fruit.
Bearing fruit or acorns, typically of a specified tincture.
examples: O beautiful for spacious skies, for amber wafes of grain, for purple mountain majesties above the fruited plain!
Jim, importuned, had come with his axe and at her wish had felled it with the fruited but unripe mistletoe.

senses: A Hindu prince or ruler in India.
ety: Borrowed from Hindi राजा (rājā) and Urdu راجا (rājā), from Sanskrit राजन् (rājan, “king, prince”), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hrā́ȷ́ā (“king”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrā́ȷ́ā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rḗǵ-ō, from *h₃rḗǵs (“ruler, king”). Doublet of Rex, rex, and roy.

senses: Synonym of sifu: the Mandarin Chinese-derived name.
ety: From the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of the Mandarin 師傅 /师傅 and 師父／师父 (shīfu).
examples: I thank Shifu Dr. Hong, Tao-Tze and my Tai Ji Men brothers and sisters because Shifu teaches me to respect each other and do things to help other people and Tai Ji Men brothers and sisters look after me and help me.

senses: A person or thing that pressurizes.
A concept in Indian music, comparable to a note or tone.
A forest of such shrubs or trees.
ety: A modification of earlier mangrowe (obsolete) by the influence of grove (“small forest”) through folk etymology. Mangrowe is probably borrowed from Spanish mangle, mangue (whence English mangle) (probably from an Arawak language (such as Taíno), or a Cariban language) + an unknown word ending.

senses: One who courts; one who plays the lover, or solicits in marriage.
Governed by (or as if by) a matriarch.
Governed by females, rather than by males.
Tending to produce crime or criminals.
Characterized by turns or a turning motion.
examples: Also, I should ask about what the turny knob tool was, when I got time.

senses: The rate of seropositivity in a population; the proportion of a population whose blood serum tests positive for a given pathogen, especially HIV.
A packrat (kind of rodent).
An umbrella term for various popular Latin American music genres.
ety: From Spanish urbano, from Spanish música urbana.
examples: With so many flavors, the album may be a sign that KAROL G is transitioning from the world of urbano to the broader category of Latin pop.

Insect-like.

Having a tendency to dissolve social connections; unsuited to society; unsociable.
ety: From Latin dissociābilis, from dissociare: compare English dissociable. See dissociate.
examples: They came in two and two, though matched in the most dissociable manner.

senses: A detachable lock that can be used to secure something by means of a sliding or hinged shackle
ety: From earlier pad lock (19th c.); Middle English padlock, padlokke, from pad-, of unknown origin, + lok (“lock”). Perhaps originally a lock for a pad (“gate”), or a gate opening to a path, or a lock for a basket or pannier, from UK dialect pad (“a pannier”).

senses: Descriptive of a style of volcanic eruption similar in character and in intensity to that of the AD 79 eruption of Vesuvius witnessed by Pliny the Younger.
examples: The earliest activity of Monte Vulture, central Italy, included ignimbrites but the bulk of the volcano was built up by plinian airfall deposits.

senses: The phenomenon of merging and converging cultures.
ety: From trans- + culture + -ation, coined by Cuban anthropologist Fernando Ortiz in 1947.

senses: A device found in a freezer that is used to make ice.

A particular profession in the production of comics, an artist specializing in neatly writing written material such as dialogue.
A device for printing letters of text.
A mixture of turpentine and egg yolk, formerly used as an emulsion.
ety: Borrowed from Latin colostrum, of uncertain origin.

senses: Happening so slowly as to appear to be static
A type of bell, usually constructed of brass, used in Hindu rituals.
examples: The ghantas are hand bells and represent the wisdom the practitioner is attempting to cultivate.

senses: A young woman.
ety: From tootsy-wootsy, originally a playful or nursery name for a small foot, from childish pronunciation of foot.
